v: The Song of Songs, which is Solomon's.[^1]
שִׁ֥יר הַשִּׁירִ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר לִשְׁלֹמֹֽה׃
Let him kiss me with the kisses of his mouth![^2] For your love[^3] is better than wine.
יִשָּׁקֵ֙נִי֙ מִנְּשִׁיק֣וֹת פִּ֔יהוּ כִּֽי־טוֹבִ֥ים דֹּדֶ֖יךָ מִיָּֽיִן׃
Your oils have a pleasing fragrance; your name is oil poured out.[^4] That is why the young women love you.
לְרֵ֙יחַ֙ שְׁמָנֶ֣יךָ טוֹבִ֔ים שֶׁ֖מֶן תּוּרַ֣ק שְׁמֶ֑ךָ עַל־כֵּ֖ן עֲלָמ֥וֹת אֲהֵבֽוּךָ׃
Draw me after you; let us run! The king has brought me into his rooms. We will rejoice and be glad in you;[^5] we will praise your love more than wine. How rightly they love you![^6]
מָשְׁכֵ֖נִי אַחֲרֶ֣יךָ נָּר֑וּצָה הֱבִיאַ֨נִי הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ חֲדָרָ֗יו נָגִ֤ילָה וְנִשְׂמְחָה֙ בָּ֔ךְ נַזְכִּ֤ירָה דֹדֶ֙יךָ֙ מִיַּ֔יִן מֵישָׁרִ֖ים אֲהֵבֽוּךָ׃ ס
I am dark, and lovely,[^7] daughters of Jerusalem, like the tents of Kedar,[^8] like the curtains of Solomon.
שְׁחוֹרָ֤ה אֲנִי֙ וְֽנָאוָ֔ה בְּנ֖וֹת יְרוּשָׁלָ֑͏ִם כְּאָהֳלֵ֣י קֵדָ֔ר כִּירִיע֖וֹת שְׁלֹמֹֽה׃
Do not stare at me because I am dark, because the sun has gazed on me. My mother's sons were angry with me; they made me keep the vineyards, but my own vineyard I have not kept.[^9]
אַל־תִּרְא֙וּנִי֙ שֶׁאֲנִ֣י שְׁחַרְחֹ֔רֶת שֶׁשֱּׁזָפַ֖תְנִי הַשָּׁ֑מֶשׁ בְּנֵ֧י אִמִּ֣י נִֽחֲרוּ־בִ֗י שָׂמֻ֙נִי֙ נֹטֵרָ֣ה אֶת־הַכְּרָמִ֔ים כַּרְמִ֥י שֶׁלִּ֖י לֹ֥א נָטָֽרְתִּי׃

Tell me, you whom my soul loves,[^10] where do you pasture your flock? Where do you make it lie down at noon? For why should I be like a woman who veils herself[^11] beside the flocks of your companions?
הַגִּ֣ידָה לִּ֗י שֶׁ֤אָהֲבָה֙ נַפְשִׁ֔י אֵיכָ֣ה תִרְעֶ֔ה אֵיכָ֖ה תַּרְבִּ֣יץ בַּֽצָּהֳרָ֑יִם שַׁלָּמָ֤ה אֶֽהְיֶה֙ כְּעֹ֣טְיָ֔ה עַ֖ל עֶדְרֵ֥י חֲבֵרֶֽיךָ׃
If you do not know,[^12] most beautiful of women, follow the tracks of the flock, and pasture your young goats beside the shepherds' tents.
אִם־לֹ֤א תֵדְעִי֙ לָ֔ךְ הַיָּפָ֖ה בַּנָּשִׁ֑ים צְֽאִי־לָ֞ךְ בְּעִקְבֵ֣י הַצֹּ֗אן וּרְעִי֙ אֶת־גְּדִיֹּתַ֔יִךְ עַ֖ל מִשְׁכְּנ֥וֹת הָרֹעִֽים׃ ס
To a mare[^13] among Pharaoh's chariots I compare you, my darling.[^14]
לְסֻסָתִי֙ בְּרִכְבֵ֣י פַרְעֹ֔ה דִּמִּיתִ֖יךְ רַעְיָתִֽי׃
Your cheeks are lovely with ornaments, your neck with strings of beads.
נָאו֤וּ לְחָיַ֙יִךְ֙ בַּתֹּרִ֔ים צַוָּארֵ֖ךְ בַּחֲרוּזִֽים׃
We will make you ornaments of gold, studded with silver.
תּוֹרֵ֤י זָהָב֙ נַעֲשֶׂה־לָּ֔ךְ עִ֖ם נְקֻדּ֥וֹת הַכָּֽסֶף׃
While the king was at his couch,[^15] my nard[^16] gave out its fragrance.
עַד־שֶׁ֤הַמֶּ֙לֶךְ֙ בִּמְסִבּ֔וֹ נִרְדִּ֖י נָתַ֥ן רֵיחֽוֹ׃
My beloved[^17] is to me a pouch of myrrh that lies between my breasts.[^18]
צְר֨וֹר הַמֹּ֤ר ׀ דּוֹדִי֙ לִ֔י בֵּ֥ין שָׁדַ֖י יָלִֽין׃
My beloved is to me a cluster of henna blossoms in the vineyards of En-gedi.[^19]
אֶשְׁכֹּ֨ל הַכֹּ֤פֶר ׀ דּוֹדִי֙ לִ֔י בְּכַרְמֵ֖י עֵ֥ין גֶּֽדִי׃ ס
How beautiful you are, my darling! How beautiful you are! Your eyes are doves.[^20]
הִנָּ֤ךְ יָפָה֙ רַעְיָתִ֔י הִנָּ֥ךְ יָפָ֖ה עֵינַ֥יִךְ יוֹנִֽים׃
How handsome you are, my beloved, how delightful![^21] Our bed is green with leaves.
הִנְּךָ֨ יָפֶ֤ה דוֹדִי֙ אַ֣ף נָעִ֔ים אַף־עַרְשֵׂ֖נוּ רַעֲנָנָֽה׃
The beams of our house are cedars, our rafters are junipers.[^22]
קֹר֤וֹת בָּתֵּ֙ינוּ֙ אֲרָזִ֔ים *רחיטנו **רַהִיטֵ֖נוּ בְּרוֹתִֽים׃

n.1: "Song of Songs" is a Hebrew superlative: the finest of songs. *Which is Solomon's* may also mean "for Solomon" or "about Solomon".
n.2: The Song is a series of love poems in which a woman and a man speak to each other and about each other, with other voices (the "daughters of Jerusalem" and others). The Hebrew does not say who is speaking, but its forms of "you", "I" and "my" often show whether a man or a woman speaks or is addressed. The notes give the probable speaker where it matters. Here the woman speaks, to the man ("you" is masculine), through verse 7.
n.3: Hebrew *dodim*, love shown in caresses and lovemaking. Also in verse 4.
n.5: "We" may be the young women of verse 3, or the woman and the man together. "You" is masculine.
n.8: A nomadic people of the Arabian desert, whose tents were made of black goats' hair.
n.10: Literally "whom my soul (*nephesh*) loves", that is, whom I love with all my being.
n.11: Perhaps a woman taken for a prostitute (compare Genesis 38:14–15). The Vulgate reads "one who wanders".
n.12: "You" is feminine. The man answers her, or the young women do.
n.13: Literally "my mare". Chariot horses were stallions, so a mare among them would draw every eye.
n.14: Hebrew *ra'yati*, "my companion, my friend", the man's name for the woman throughout the Song. The man speaks in verses 9–11.
n.15: Or "at his table", where guests reclined on couches. The woman speaks in verses 12–14.
n.16: A costly perfume made from a plant of the Himalayas.
n.17: Hebrew *dodi*, "my beloved", the woman's name for the man throughout the Song. It comes from the same root as *dodim*, "love", in verse 2.
n.18: Or "that spends the night between my breasts".
n.19: An oasis on the western shore of the Dead Sea.
n.21: The woman speaks ("you" is masculine) in verses 16–17.

v: I am a crocus[^1] of Sharon, a lily of the valleys.
אֲנִי֙ חֲבַצֶּ֣לֶת הַשָּׁר֔וֹן שֽׁוֹשַׁנַּ֖ת הָעֲמָקִֽים׃
Like a lily among thorns, so is my darling among the young women.[^2]
כְּשֽׁוֹשַׁנָּה֙ בֵּ֣ין הַחוֹחִ֔ים כֵּ֥ן רַעְיָתִ֖י בֵּ֥ין הַבָּנֽוֹת׃
Like an apple tree[^3] among the trees of the forest, so is my beloved among the young men. In his shade I delighted to sit, and his fruit was sweet to my taste.[^4]
כְּתַפּ֙וּחַ֙ בַּעֲצֵ֣י הַיַּ֔עַר כֵּ֥ן דּוֹדִ֖י בֵּ֣ין הַבָּנִ֑ים בְּצִלּוֹ֙ חִמַּ֣דְתִּי וְיָשַׁ֔בְתִּי וּפִרְי֖וֹ מָת֥וֹק לְחִכִּֽי׃
He brought me to the house of wine, and his banner over me was love.[^5]
הֱבִיאַ֙נִי֙ אֶל־בֵּ֣ית הַיָּ֔יִן וְדִגְל֥וֹ עָלַ֖י אַהֲבָֽה׃
Sustain me with raisin cakes, refresh me with apples,[^6] for I am sick with love.
סַמְּכ֙וּנִי֙ בָּֽאֲשִׁישׁ֔וֹת רַפְּד֖וּנִי בַּתַּפּוּחִ֑ים כִּי־חוֹלַ֥ת אַהֲבָ֖ה אָֽנִי׃
His left hand is under my head, and his right hand embraces me.
שְׂמֹאלוֹ֙ תַּ֣חַת לְרֹאשִׁ֔י וִימִינ֖וֹ תְּחַבְּקֵֽנִי׃
I make you swear, daughters of Jerusalem, by the gazelles or by the does of the field:[^7] do not stir up or awaken love until it is ready.[^8]
הִשְׁבַּ֨עְתִּי אֶתְכֶ֜ם בְּנ֤וֹת יְרוּשָׁלִַ֙ם֙ בִּצְבָא֔וֹת א֖וֹ בְּאַיְל֣וֹת הַשָּׂדֶ֑ה אִם־תָּעִ֧ירוּ ׀ וְֽאִם־תְּעֽוֹרְר֛וּ אֶת־הָאַהֲבָ֖ה עַ֥ד שֶׁתֶּחְפָּֽץ׃ ס
Listen! My beloved![^9] Look, here he comes, leaping over the mountains, bounding over the hills.
ק֣וֹל דּוֹדִ֔י הִנֵּה־זֶ֖ה בָּ֑א מְדַלֵּג֙ עַל־הֶ֣הָרִ֔ים מְקַפֵּ֖ץ עַל־הַגְּבָעֽוֹת׃
My beloved is like a gazelle or a young stag. Look, there he stands behind our wall, gazing in through the windows, peering through the lattice.
דּוֹמֶ֤ה דוֹדִי֙ לִצְבִ֔י א֖וֹ לְעֹ֣פֶר הָֽאַיָּלִ֑ים הִנֵּה־זֶ֤ה עוֹמֵד֙ אַחַ֣ר כָּתְלֵ֔נוּ מַשְׁגִּ֙יחַ֙ מִן־הַֽחֲלֹּנ֔וֹת מֵצִ֖יץ מִן־הֽ͏ַחֲרַכִּֽים׃
My beloved spoke and said to me, "Arise, my darling, my beautiful one, and come away.
עָנָ֥ה דוֹדִ֖י וְאָ֣מַר לִ֑י ק֥וּמִי לָ֛ךְ רַעְיָתִ֥י יָפָתִ֖י וּלְכִי־לָֽךְ׃
For look, the winter is past; the rain is over and gone.
כִּֽי־הִנֵּ֥ה *הסתו **הַסְּתָ֖יו עָבָ֑ר הַגֶּ֕שֶׁם חָלַ֖ף הָלַ֥ךְ לֽוֹ׃
The blossoms have appeared in the land; the time of pruning[^10] has come, and the voice of the turtledove is heard in our land.
הַנִּצָּנִים֙ נִרְא֣וּ בָאָ֔רֶץ עֵ֥ת הַזָּמִ֖יר הִגִּ֑יעַ וְק֥וֹל הַתּ֖וֹר נִשְׁמַ֥ע בְּאַרְצֵֽנוּ׃
The fig tree ripens its early figs, and the vines in blossom give out their fragrance. Arise, my darling, my beautiful one, and come away."
הַתְּאֵנָה֙ חָֽנְטָ֣ה פַגֶּ֔יהָ וְהַגְּפָנִ֥ים ׀ סְמָדַ֖ר נָ֣תְנוּ רֵ֑יחַ ק֥וּמִי *לכי **לָ֛ךְ רַעְיָתִ֥י יָפָתִ֖י וּלְכִי־לָֽךְ׃ ס
My dove, in the clefts of the rock, in the hiding places of the cliff,[^11] let me see your form, let me hear your voice, for your voice is sweet, and your form is lovely.
יוֹנָתִ֞י בְּחַגְוֵ֣י הַסֶּ֗לַע בְּסֵ֙תֶר֙ הַמַּדְרֵגָ֔ה הַרְאִ֙ינִי֙ אֶת־מַרְאַ֔יִךְ הַשְׁמִיעִ֖ינִי אֶת־קוֹלֵ֑ךְ כִּי־קוֹלֵ֥ךְ עָרֵ֖ב וּמַרְאֵ֥יךְ נָאוֶֽה׃ ס
Catch the foxes for us, the little foxes that ruin the vineyards, for our vineyards are in blossom.[^12]
אֶֽחֱזוּ־לָ֙נוּ֙ שֽׁוּעָלִ֔ים שֽׁוּעָלִ֥ים קְטַנִּ֖ים מְחַבְּלִ֣ים כְּרָמִ֑ים וּכְרָמֵ֖ינוּ סְמָדַֽר׃
My beloved is mine and I am his; he grazes among the lilies.[^13]
דּוֹדִ֥י לִי֙ וַאֲנִ֣י ל֔וֹ הָרֹעֶ֖ה בַּשּׁוֹשַׁנִּֽים׃
Until the day breathes[^14] and the shadows flee, turn, my beloved, and be like a gazelle or a young stag on the cleft mountains.[^15]
עַ֤ד שֶׁיָּפ֙וּחַ֙ הַיּ֔וֹם וְנָ֖סוּ הַצְּלָלִ֑ים סֹב֩ דְּמֵה־לְךָ֨ דוֹדִ֜י לִצְבִ֗י א֛וֹ לְעֹ֥פֶר הָאַיָּלִ֖ים עַל־הָ֥רֵי בָֽתֶר׃ ס

n.1: Hebrew *chavatselet*, a meadow flower, perhaps a crocus or an asphodel; traditionally "rose". Sharon is the coastal plain south of Mount Carmel. The woman probably speaks.
n.3: Hebrew *tappuach*, perhaps an apricot. Also in verse 5.
n.5: Or "and his look upon me was love".
n.6: The commands are plural: she speaks to the young women.
n.7: An oath by the animals of love. In Hebrew *bi-tsva'ot o be-ayelot ha-sadeh* sounds like the oaths "by (the LORD of) Armies", *tseva'ot*, and "by God Almighty", *El Shaddai*. The same refrain comes in 3:5, and in a shorter form in 8:4.
n.10: Or "the time of singing". Hebrew *zamir* can mean either.
n.11: The man's words go on, either still quoted by the woman or spoken by him ("your" is feminine). Literally "in the hiding place of the steep slope".
n.12: Who speaks is not clear; the command is plural.
n.13: Or "he pastures his flock among the lilies".
n.14: That is, until the cool breeze of evening, or until the dawn.
n.15: Or "on the mountains of Bether". Hebrew *bater* means "division, cleft". Compare 8:14.

v: On my bed, night after night,[^1] I sought the one my soul loves;[^2] I sought him, but did not find him.
עַל־מִשְׁכָּבִי֙ בַּלֵּיל֔וֹת בִּקַּ֕שְׁתִּי אֵ֥ת שֶׁאָהֲבָ֖ה נַפְשִׁ֑י בִּקַּשְׁתִּ֖יו וְלֹ֥א מְצָאתִֽיו׃
I will get up now and go around the city, through the streets and through the squares; I will seek the one my soul loves. I sought him, but did not find him.
אָק֨וּמָה נָּ֜א וַאֲסוֹבְבָ֣ה בָעִ֗יר בַּשְּׁוָקִים֙ וּבָ֣רְחֹב֔וֹת אֲבַקְשָׁ֕ה אֵ֥ת שֶׁאָהֲבָ֖ה נַפְשִׁ֑י בִּקַּשְׁתִּ֖יו וְלֹ֥א מְצָאתִֽיו׃
The watchmen found me as they went around the city. "Have you seen the one my soul loves?"
מְצָא֙וּנִי֙ הַשֹּׁ֣מְרִ֔ים הַסֹּבְבִ֖ים בָּעִ֑יר אֵ֛ת שֶׁאָהֲבָ֥ה נַפְשִׁ֖י רְאִיתֶֽם׃
Scarcely had I passed them when I found the one my soul loves. I held him and would not let him go until I had brought him into my mother's house, into the room of the one who conceived me.
כִּמְעַט֙ שֶׁעָבַ֣רְתִּי מֵהֶ֔ם עַ֣ד שֶֽׁמָּצָ֔אתִי אֵ֥ת שֶׁאָהֲבָ֖ה נַפְשִׁ֑י אֲחַזְתִּיו֙ וְלֹ֣א אַרְפֶּ֔נּוּ עַד־שֶׁ֤הֲבֵיאתִיו֙ אֶל־בֵּ֣ית אִמִּ֔י וְאֶל־חֶ֖דֶר הוֹרָתִֽי׃
I make you swear, daughters of Jerusalem, by the gazelles or by the does of the field:[^3] do not stir up or awaken love until it is ready.
הִשְׁבַּ֨עְתִּי אֶתְכֶ֜ם בְּנ֤וֹת יְרוּשָׁלִַ֙ם֙ בִּצְבָא֔וֹת א֖וֹ בְּאַיְל֣וֹת הַשָּׂדֶ֑ה אִם־תָּעִ֧ירוּ ׀ וְֽאִם־תְּעֽוֹרְר֛וּ אֶת־הָאַהֲבָ֖ה עַ֥ד שֶׁתֶּחְפָּֽץ׃ ס
Who is this coming up from the wilderness like columns of smoke,[^4] perfumed with myrrh and frankincense, with all the powders of the merchant?
מִ֣י זֹ֗את עֹלָה֙ מִן־הַמִּדְבָּ֔ר כְּתִֽימֲר֖וֹת עָשָׁ֑ן מְקֻטֶּ֤רֶת מוֹר֙ וּלְבוֹנָ֔ה מִכֹּ֖ל אַבְקַ֥ת רוֹכֵֽל׃
Look, it is Solomon's couch![^5] Sixty warriors surround it, from the warriors of Israel.
הִנֵּ֗ה מִטָּתוֹ֙ שֶׁלִּשְׁלֹמֹ֔ה שִׁשִּׁ֥ים גִּבֹּרִ֖ים סָבִ֣יב לָ֑הּ מִגִּבֹּרֵ֖י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
All of them hold swords and are trained in battle, each with his sword at his side,[^6] against the terrors of the night.
כֻּלָּם֙ אֲחֻ֣זֵי חֶ֔רֶב מְלֻמְּדֵ֖י מִלְחָמָ֑ה אִ֤ישׁ חַרְבּוֹ֙ עַל־יְרֵכ֔וֹ מִפַּ֖חַד בַּלֵּילּֽוֹת׃ ס
King Solomon made himself a carriage[^7] from the wood of Lebanon.
אַפִּרְי֗וֹן עָ֤שָׂה לוֹ֙ הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה מֵעֲצֵ֖י הַלְּבָנֽוֹן׃
He made its posts of silver, its back of gold, its seat of purple; its inside was inlaid with love by the daughters of Jerusalem.[^8]
עַמּוּדָיו֙ עָ֣שָׂה כֶ֔סֶף רְפִידָת֣וֹ זָהָ֔ב מֶרְכָּב֖וֹ אַרְגָּמָ֑ן תּוֹכוֹ֙ רָצ֣וּף אַהֲבָ֔ה מִבְּנ֖וֹת יְרוּשָׁלָֽ͏ִם׃
Go out and look, daughters of Zion, at King Solomon, at the crown with which his mother crowned him on the day of his wedding, on the day of his heart's joy.
צְאֶ֧ינָה ׀ וּֽרְאֶ֛ינָה בְּנ֥וֹת צִיּ֖וֹן בַּמֶּ֣לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹ֑ה בָּעֲטָרָ֗ה שֶׁעִטְּרָה־לּ֤וֹ אִמּוֹ֙ בְּי֣וֹם חֲתֻנָּת֔וֹ וּבְי֖וֹם שִׂמְחַ֥ת לִבּֽוֹ׃ ס

n.1: Literally "in the nights". The woman speaks in verses 1–5.
n.2: Literally "whom my soul (*nephesh*) loves"; see 1:7. Also in verses 2–4.
n.4: "Who" is feminine in the Hebrew. It may refer to the woman, or to Solomon's couch (verse 7), a feminine word.
n.5: Hebrew *mittah*, a bed or couch, here one carried in procession.
n.7: Hebrew *appiryon*, a word found only here, probably borrowed from another language: a sedan chair or palanquin.
n.8: Literally "its inside inlaid, love, from the daughters of Jerusalem". Or "inlaid with love for the daughters of Jerusalem".

v: How beautiful you are, my darling![^1] How beautiful you are! Your eyes are doves behind your veil. Your hair is like a flock of goats streaming down from Mount Gilead.
הִנָּ֨ךְ יָפָ֤ה רַעְיָתִי֙ הִנָּ֣ךְ יָפָ֔ה עֵינַ֣יִךְ יוֹנִ֔ים מִבַּ֖עַד לְצַמָּתֵ֑ךְ שַׂעְרֵךְ֙ כְּעֵ֣דֶר הָֽעִזִּ֔ים שֶׁגָּלְשׁ֖וּ מֵהַ֥ר גִּלְעָֽד׃
Your teeth are like a flock of shorn ewes that have come up from the washing; all of them bear twins, and not one among them has lost its young.
שִׁנַּ֙יִךְ֙ כְּעֵ֣דֶר הַקְּצוּב֔וֹת שֶׁעָל֖וּ מִן־הָרַחְצָ֑ה שֶׁכֻּלָּם֙ מַתְאִימ֔וֹת וְשַׁכֻּלָ֖ה אֵ֥ין בָּהֶֽם׃
Your lips are like a scarlet thread, and your mouth is lovely. Your temples[^2] are like a slice of pomegranate behind your veil.
כְּח֤וּט הַשָּׁנִי֙ שִׂפְתֹתַ֔יִךְ וּמִדְבָּרֵ֖יךְ נָאוֶ֑ה כְּפֶ֤לַח הָֽרִמּוֹן֙ רַקָּתֵ֔ךְ מִבַּ֖עַד לְצַמָּתֵֽךְ׃
Your neck is like the tower of David, built in courses,[^3] on which hang a thousand shields, all the shields of warriors.
כְּמִגְדַּ֤ל דָּוִיד֙ צַוָּארֵ֔ךְ בָּנ֖וּי לְתַלְפִּיּ֑וֹת אֶ֤לֶף הַמָּגֵן֙ תָּל֣וּי עָלָ֔יו כֹּ֖ל שִׁלְטֵ֥י הַגִּבּוֹרִֽים׃
Your two breasts are like two fawns, twins of a gazelle, that graze among the lilies.
שְׁנֵ֥י שָׁדַ֛יִךְ כִּשְׁנֵ֥י עֳפָרִ֖ים תְּאוֹמֵ֣י צְבִיָּ֑ה הָרוֹעִ֖ים בַּשּׁוֹשַׁנִּֽים׃
Until the day breathes[^4] and the shadows flee, I will go to the mountain of myrrh and to the hill of frankincense.
עַ֤ד שֶׁיָּפ֙וּחַ֙ הַיּ֔וֹם וְנָ֖סוּ הַצְּלָלִ֑ים אֵ֤לֶךְ לִי֙ אֶל־הַ֣ר הַמּ֔וֹר וְאֶל־גִּבְעַ֖ת הַלְּבוֹנָֽה׃
You are altogether beautiful, my darling; there is no flaw in you.
כֻּלָּ֤ךְ יָפָה֙ רַעְיָתִ֔י וּמ֖וּם אֵ֥ין בָּֽךְ׃ ס
Come with me from Lebanon, my bride, come with me from Lebanon. Look down[^5] from the peak of Amana, from the peak of Senir and Hermon,[^6] from the dens of lions, from the mountains of leopards.
אִתִּ֤י מִלְּבָנוֹן֙ כַּלָּ֔ה אִתִּ֖י מִלְּבָנ֣וֹן תָּב֑וֹאִי תָּשׁ֣וּרִי ׀ מֵרֹ֣אשׁ אֲמָנָ֗ה מֵרֹ֤אשׁ שְׂנִיר֙ וְחֶרְמ֔וֹן מִמְּעֹנ֣וֹת אֲרָי֔וֹת מֵֽהַרְרֵ֖י נְמֵרִֽים׃
You have stolen my heart,[^7] my sister,[^8] my bride; you have stolen my heart with one glance of your eyes, with one jewel of your necklace.
לִבַּבְתִּ֖נִי אֲחֹתִ֣י כַלָּ֑ה לִבַּבְתִּ֙ינִי֙ *באחד **בְּאַחַ֣ת מֵעֵינַ֔יִךְ בְּאַחַ֥ד עֲנָ֖ק מִצַּוְּרֹנָֽיִךְ׃
How beautiful is your love,[^9] my sister, my bride! How much better is your love than wine, and the fragrance of your oils than any spice!
מַה־יָּפ֥וּ דֹדַ֖יִךְ אֲחֹתִ֣י כַלָּ֑ה מַה־טֹּ֤בוּ דֹדַ֙יִךְ֙ מִיַּ֔יִן וְרֵ֥יחַ שְׁמָנַ֖יִךְ מִכָּל־בְּשָׂמִֽים׃
Your lips drip honey from the comb, my bride; honey and milk are under your tongue, and the fragrance of your garments is like the fragrance of Lebanon.
נֹ֛פֶת תִּטֹּ֥פְנָה שִׂפְתוֹתַ֖יִךְ כַּלָּ֑ה דְּבַ֤שׁ וְחָלָב֙ תַּ֣חַת לְשׁוֹנֵ֔ךְ וְרֵ֥יחַ שַׂלְמֹתַ֖יִךְ כְּרֵ֥יחַ לְבָנֽוֹן׃ ס
A garden locked is my sister, my bride, a pool[^10] locked, a fountain sealed.
גַּ֥ן ׀ נָע֖וּל אֲחֹתִ֣י כַלָּ֑ה גַּ֥ל נָע֖וּל מַעְיָ֥ן חָתֽוּם׃
Your shoots[^11] are a park[^12] of pomegranates with choice fruits, henna with nard,
שְׁלָחַ֙יִךְ֙ פַּרְדֵּ֣ס רִמּוֹנִ֔ים עִ֖ם פְּרִ֣י מְגָדִ֑ים כְּפָרִ֖ים עִם־נְרָדִֽים׃
nard and saffron, cane and cinnamon, with every kind of incense tree, myrrh and aloes, with all the finest spices.
נֵ֣רְדְּ ׀ וְכַרְכֹּ֗ם קָנֶה֙ וְקִנָּמ֔וֹן עִ֖ם כָּל־עֲצֵ֣י לְבוֹנָ֑ה מֹ֚ר וַאֲהָל֔וֹת עִ֖ם כָּל־רָאשֵׁ֥י בְשָׂמִֽים׃
You are a fountain in the gardens, a well of living water,[^13] streams flowing down from Lebanon.
מַעְיַ֣ן גַּנִּ֔ים בְּאֵ֖ר מַ֣יִם חַיִּ֑ים וְנֹזְלִ֖ים מִן־לְבָנֽוֹן׃
Awake, north wind, and come, south wind! Blow on my garden, let its spices flow.[^14] Let my beloved come into his garden and eat its choice fruits.
ע֤וּרִי צָפוֹן֙ וּב֣וֹאִי תֵימָ֔ן הָפִ֥יחִי גַנִּ֖י יִזְל֣וּ בְשָׂמָ֑יו יָבֹ֤א דוֹדִי֙ לְגַנּ֔וֹ וְיֹאכַ֖ל פְּרִ֥י מְגָדָֽיו׃

n.1: The man speaks ("you" is feminine) in verses 1–15.
n.3: Hebrew *le-talpiyyot*, a word found only here, of uncertain meaning: perhaps "in courses (of stone)", "for an armory", or "with turrets".
n.6: Amana is a peak of the Anti-Lebanon range. Senir is another name for Hermon (Deuteronomy 3:9), or a peak near it.
n.7: Hebrew *libbavtini*, from *lev*, "heart". Or "You have made my heart beat faster".
n.8: An affectionate name for a beloved woman, as in ancient Egyptian love songs. Also in verses 10 and 12.
n.9: Hebrew *dodim*; see 1:2. Also later in the verse.
n.10: Hebrew *gal*, perhaps "pool" or "spring". The Septuagint and the Vulgate read "a garden", as in the first line.
n.11: Or "Your channels". Hebrew *shelachayikh*, perhaps the shoots of a plant or the channels that water a garden.
n.12: Hebrew *pardes*, a Persian word for an enclosed park, the source of the English word "paradise".
n.14: Who speaks the first half of the verse is not clear: the man, or the woman calling her body "my garden". In the second half the woman speaks ("my beloved").

v: I have come into my garden, my sister, my bride;[^1] I have gathered my myrrh with my spice, I have eaten my honeycomb[^2] with my honey, I have drunk my wine with my milk. Eat, friends, drink, and be drunk with love![^3]
בָּ֣אתִי לְגַנִּי֮ אֲחֹתִ֣י כַלָּה֒ אָרִ֤יתִי מוֹרִי֙ עִם־בְּשָׂמִ֔י אָכַ֤לְתִּי יַעְרִי֙ עִם־דִּבְשִׁ֔י שָׁתִ֥יתִי יֵינִ֖י עִם־חֲלָבִ֑י אִכְל֣וּ רֵעִ֔ים שְׁת֥וּ וְשִׁכְר֖וּ דּוֹדִֽים׃ ס

I was asleep, but my heart was awake.[^4] Listen! My beloved is knocking.[^5] "Open to me, my sister, my darling, my dove, my perfect one, for my head is wet with dew, my locks with the drops of the night."
אֲנִ֥י יְשֵׁנָ֖ה וְלִבִּ֣י עֵ֑ר ק֣וֹל ׀ דּוֹדִ֣י דוֹפֵ֗ק פִּתְחִי־לִ֞י אֲחֹתִ֤י רַעְיָתִי֙ יוֹנָתִ֣י תַמָּתִ֔י שֶׁרֹּאשִׁי֙ נִמְלָא־טָ֔ל קְוֻּצּוֹתַ֖י רְסִ֥יסֵי לָֽיְלָה׃
I have taken off my robe; how could I put it on again? I have washed my feet; how could I soil them?
פָּשַׁ֙טְתִּי֙ אֶת־כֻּתָּנְתִּ֔י אֵיכָ֖כָה אֶלְבָּשֶׁ֑נָּה רָחַ֥צְתִּי אֶת־רַגְלַ֖י אֵיכָ֥כָה אֲטַנְּפֵֽם׃
My beloved put his hand in through the opening,[^6] and my heart[^7] trembled for him.
דּוֹדִ֗י שָׁלַ֤ח יָדוֹ֙ מִן־הַחֹ֔ר וּמֵעַ֖י הָמ֥וּ עָלָֽיו׃
I rose to open to my beloved, and my hands dripped with myrrh, my fingers with flowing myrrh, on the handles of the bolt.
קַ֥מְתִּֽי אֲנִ֖י לִפְתֹּ֣חַ לְדוֹדִ֑י וְיָדַ֣י נָֽטְפוּ־מ֗וֹר וְאֶצְבְּעֹתַי֙ מ֣וֹר עֹבֵ֔ר עַ֖ל כַּפּ֥וֹת הַמַּנְעֽוּל׃
I opened to my beloved, but my beloved had turned and gone. My soul went out when he spoke.[^8] I sought him, but did not find him; I called him, but he did not answer me.
פָּתַ֤חְתִּֽי אֲנִי֙ לְדוֹדִ֔י וְדוֹדִ֖י חָמַ֣ק עָבָ֑ר נַפְשִׁי֙ יָֽצְאָ֣ה בְדַבְּר֔וֹ בִּקַּשְׁתִּ֙יהוּ֙ וְלֹ֣א מְצָאתִ֔יהוּ קְרָאתִ֖יו וְלֹ֥א עָנָֽנִי׃
The watchmen found me as they went around the city. They struck me, they wounded me; they took my shawl from me, those watchmen of the walls.
מְצָאֻ֧נִי הַשֹּׁמְרִ֛ים הַסֹּבְבִ֥ים בָּעִ֖יר הִכּ֣וּנִי פְצָע֑וּנִי נָשְׂא֤וּ אֶת־רְדִידִי֙ מֵֽעָלַ֔י שֹׁמְרֵ֖י הַחֹמֽוֹת׃
I make you swear, daughters of Jerusalem: if you find my beloved, what will you tell him? That I am sick with love.
הִשְׁבַּ֥עְתִּי אֶתְכֶ֖ם בְּנ֣וֹת יְרוּשָׁלָ֑͏ִם אִֽם־תִּמְצְאוּ֙ אֶת־דּוֹדִ֔י מַה־תַּגִּ֣ידוּ ל֔וֹ שֶׁחוֹלַ֥ת אַהֲבָ֖ה אָֽנִי׃
What is your beloved more than any other beloved, most beautiful of women? What is your beloved more than any other beloved, that you make us swear like this?[^9]
מַה־דּוֹדֵ֣ךְ מִדּ֔וֹד הַיָּפָ֖ה בַּנָּשִׁ֑ים מַה־דּוֹדֵ֣ךְ מִדּ֔וֹד שֶׁכָּ֖כָה הִשְׁבַּעְתָּֽנוּ׃
My beloved is radiant and ruddy,[^10] outstanding among ten thousand.
דּוֹדִ֥י צַח֙ וְאָד֔וֹם דָּג֖וּל מֵרְבָבָֽה׃
His head is the finest gold; his locks are wavy,[^11] black as a raven.
רֹאשׁ֖וֹ כֶּ֣תֶם פָּ֑ז קְוּצּוֹתָיו֙ תַּלְתַּלִּ֔ים שְׁחֹר֖וֹת כָּעוֹרֵֽב׃
His eyes are like doves beside streams of water, bathed in milk, sitting by brimming pools.[^12]
עֵינָ֕יו כְּיוֹנִ֖ים עַל־אֲפִ֣יקֵי מָ֑יִם רֹֽחֲצוֹת֙ בֶּֽחָלָ֔ב יֹשְׁב֖וֹת עַל־מִלֵּֽאת׃
His cheeks are like beds of spices, towers of perfume.[^13] His lips are lilies, dripping with flowing myrrh.
לְחָיָו֙ כַּעֲרוּגַ֣ת הַבֹּ֔שֶׂם מִגְדְּל֖וֹת מֶרְקָחִ֑ים שִׂפְתוֹתָיו֙ שֽׁוֹשַׁנִּ֔ים נֹטְפ֖וֹת מ֥וֹר עֹבֵֽר׃
His arms[^14] are rods of gold set with jewels of Tarshish.[^15] His body is polished ivory, covered with sapphires.[^16]
יָדָיו֙ גְּלִילֵ֣י זָהָ֔ב מְמֻלָּאִ֖ים בַּתַּרְשִׁ֑ישׁ מֵעָיו֙ עֶ֣שֶׁת שֵׁ֔ן מְעֻלֶּ֖פֶת סַפִּירִֽים׃
His legs are pillars of alabaster,[^17] set on bases of fine gold. His appearance is like Lebanon, choice as the cedars.
שׁוֹקָיו֙ עַמּ֣וּדֵי שֵׁ֔שׁ מְיֻסָּדִ֖ים עַל־אַדְנֵי־פָ֑ז מַרְאֵ֙הוּ֙ כַּלְּבָנ֔וֹן בָּח֖וּר כָּאֲרָזִֽים׃
His mouth[^18] is sweetness itself, and he is altogether desirable. This is my beloved and this is my friend,[^19] daughters of Jerusalem.
חִכּוֹ֙ מַֽמְתַקִּ֔ים וְכֻלּ֖וֹ מַחֲ[t]מַדִּ֑ים זֶ֤ה דוֹדִי֙ וְזֶ֣ה רֵעִ֔י בְּנ֖וֹת יְרוּשָׁלָֽ͏ִם׃

n.1: The man speaks ("my sister, my bride"); see 4:9.
n.2: Hebrew *ya'ar*, usually "forest", here "honeycomb", as in 1 Samuel 14:27.
n.3: Or "drink deeply, you lovers!" Hebrew *dodim* can mean "love" (1:2) or "lovers". Who speaks this line is not clear: the man, or another voice.
n.5: Literally "The voice of my beloved knocking!"
n.6: Literally "the hole", perhaps the opening for the key or latch.
n.8: Literally "My soul (*nephesh*) went out at his speaking". Or "My heart sank at his leaving".
n.9: The daughters of Jerusalem speak ("your" is feminine, and "us").
n.11: Hebrew *taltallim*, a word found only here, perhaps "wavy", "curly", or "like clusters of dates".
n.12: Literally "sitting on fullness": perhaps by full pools, or set like gems in their setting.
n.13: With different vowels, the Hebrew can be read "that produce perfume", as the Septuagint reads.
n.15: A precious stone, perhaps named after the faraway land of Tarshish: perhaps beryl or topaz.
n.16: Hebrew *sappirim*, probably lapis lazuli, a deep blue stone.
n.19: Hebrew *re'i*, the masculine form of *ra'yati*, "my darling" (1:9).

v: Where has your beloved gone, most beautiful of women? Where has your beloved turned, that we may seek him with you?[^1]
אָ֚נָה הָלַ֣ךְ דּוֹדֵ֔ךְ הַיָּפָ֖ה בַּנָּשִׁ֑ים אָ֚נָה פָּנָ֣ה דוֹדֵ֔ךְ וּנְבַקְשֶׁ֖נּוּ עִמָּֽךְ׃
My beloved has gone down to his garden, to the beds of spices, to graze in the gardens and to gather lilies.[^2]
דּוֹדִי֙ יָרַ֣ד לְגַנּ֔וֹ לַעֲרוּג֖וֹת הַבֹּ֑שֶׂם לִרְעוֹת֙ בַּגַּנִּ֔ים וְלִלְקֹ֖ט שֽׁוֹשַׁנִּֽים׃
I am my beloved's and my beloved is mine; he grazes among the lilies.
אֲנִ֤י לְדוֹדִי֙ וְדוֹדִ֣י לִ֔י הָרֹעֶ֖ה בַּשׁוֹשַׁנִּֽים׃ ס
You are beautiful, my darling, as Tirzah,[^3] lovely as Jerusalem, awe-inspiring as armies with banners.[^4]
יָפָ֨ה אַ֤תְּ רַעְיָתִי֙ כְּתִרְצָ֔ה נָאוָ֖ה כִּירוּשָׁלָ֑͏ִם אֲיֻמָּ֖ה כַּנִּדְגָּלֽוֹת׃
Turn your eyes away from me, for they overwhelm me. Your hair is like a flock of goats streaming down from Gilead.
הָסֵ֤בִּי עֵינַ֙יִךְ֙ מִנֶּגְדִּ֔י שֶׁ֥הֵ֖ם הִרְהִיבֻ֑נִי שַׂעְרֵךְ֙ כְּעֵ֣דֶר הָֽעִזִּ֔ים שֶׁגָּלְשׁ֖וּ מִן־הַגִּלְעָֽד׃
Your teeth are like a flock of ewes that have come up from the washing; all of them bear twins, and not one among them has lost its young.
שִׁנַּ֙יִךְ֙ כְּעֵ֣דֶר הֽ͏ָרְחֵלִ֔ים שֶׁעָל֖וּ מִן־הָרַחְצָ֑ה שֶׁכֻּלָּם֙ מַתְאִימ֔וֹת וְשַׁכֻּלָ֖ה אֵ֥ין בָּהֶֽם׃
Your temples are like a slice of pomegranate behind your veil.
כְּפֶ֤לַח הָרִמּוֹן֙ רַקָּתֵ֔ךְ מִבַּ֖עַד לְצַמָּתֵֽךְ׃
There are sixty queens and eighty concubines, and young women without number.
שִׁשִּׁ֥ים הֵ֙מָּה֙ מְּ[c]לָכ֔וֹת וּשְׁמֹנִ֖ים פִּֽילַגְשִׁ֑ים וַעֲלָמ֖וֹת אֵ֥ין מִסְפָּֽר׃

But my dove, my perfect one, is the only one, the only one of her mother, the favorite of the one who bore her. The young women saw her and called her blessed; the queens and concubines saw her and praised her:[^5]
אַחַ֥ת הִיא֙ יוֹנָתִ֣י תַמָּתִ֔י אַחַ֥ת הִיא֙ לְאִמָּ֔הּ בָּרָ֥ה הִ֖יא לְיֽוֹלַדְתָּ֑הּ רָא֤וּהָ בָנוֹת֙ וַֽיְאַשְּׁר֔וּהָ מְלָכ֥וֹת וּפִֽילַגְשִׁ֖ים וַֽיְהַלְלֽוּהָ׃ ס
Who is this who looks down like the dawn, beautiful as the moon, bright as the sun,[^6] awe-inspiring as armies with banners?
מִי־זֹ֥את הַנִּשְׁקָפָ֖ה כְּמוֹ־שָׁ֑חַר יָפָ֣ה כַלְּבָנָ֗ה בָּרָה֙ כַּֽחַמָּ֔ה אֲיֻמָּ֖ה כַּנִּדְגָּלֽוֹת׃ ס
I went down to the walnut grove to look at the green shoots of the valley,[^7] to see whether the vine had budded, whether the pomegranates were in bloom.[^8]
אֶל־גִּנַּ֤ת אֱגוֹז֙ יָרַ֔דְתִּי לִרְא֖וֹת בְּאִבֵּ֣י הַנָּ֑חַל לִרְאוֹת֙ הֲפָֽרְחָ֣ה הַגֶּ֔פֶן הֵנֵ֖צוּ הָרִמֹּנִֽים׃
Before I knew it, my desire set me among the chariots of my noble people.[^9]
לֹ֣א יָדַ֔עְתִּי נַפְשִׁ֣י שָׂמַ֔תְנִי מַרְכְּב֖וֹת עַמִּי־נָדִֽיב׃

n.1: The daughters of Jerusalem speak ("your" is feminine).
n.3: An early capital of the northern kingdom of Israel (1 Kings 14:17; 16:23). The name means "pleasing". The man speaks in verses 4–10 ("you" is feminine).
n.4: Hebrew *ka-nidgalot*, "like those with banners": perhaps armies, or the stars. Also in verse 10.
n.5: Literally "and they praised her". Verse 10 may give the words of their praise.
n.6: Hebrew *levanah*, "the white one", and *chammah*, "the hot one", poetic words for the moon and the sun.
n.7: Hebrew *nachal*, a valley with a stream that flows in the rainy season.
n.8: Who speaks in verses 11–12 is not clear: perhaps the woman, perhaps the man.
n.9: The Hebrew is very obscure. Literally "I did not know, my soul set me chariots of my people, noble". Or "the chariots of Amminadib", taking the last words as a name.

v: Turn back, turn back, O Shulammite![^1] Turn back, turn back, that we may look at you! Why would you look at the Shulammite, as at the dance of the two camps?[^2]
שׁ֤וּבִי שׁ֙וּבִי֙ הַשּׁ֣וּלַמִּ֔ית שׁ֥וּבִי שׁ֖וּבִי וְנֶחֱזֶה־בָּ֑ךְ מַֽה־תֶּחֱזוּ֙ בַּשּׁ֣וּלַמִּ֔ית כִּמְחֹלַ֖ת הַֽמַּחֲנָֽיִם׃
How beautiful are your feet in sandals, O noble daughter![^3] The curves of your thighs are like jewels, the work of a craftsman's hands.
מַה־יָּפ֧וּ פְעָמַ֛יִךְ בַּנְּעָלִ֖ים בַּת־נָדִ֑יב חַמּוּקֵ֣י יְרֵכַ֔יִךְ כְּמ֣וֹ חֲלָאִ֔ים מַעֲשֵׂ֖ה יְדֵ֥י אָמָּֽן׃
Your navel is a rounded bowl; may it never lack mixed wine.[^4] Your belly is a heap of wheat, encircled with lilies.
שָׁרְרֵךְ֙ אַגַּ֣ן הַסַּ֔הַר אַל־יֶחְסַ֖ר הַמָּ֑זֶג בִּטְנֵךְ֙ עֲרֵמַ֣ת חִטִּ֔ים סוּגָ֖ה בַּשּׁוֹשַׁנִּֽים׃
Your two breasts are like two fawns, twins of a gazelle.
שְׁנֵ֥י שָׁדַ֛יִךְ כִּשְׁנֵ֥י עֳפָרִ֖ים תָּאֳמֵ֥י צְבִיָּֽה׃
Your neck is like a tower of ivory. Your eyes are pools in Heshbon,[^5] by the gate of Bath-rabbim.[^6] Your nose is like the tower of Lebanon, looking out toward Damascus.
צַוָּארֵ֖ךְ כְּמִגְדַּ֣ל הַשֵּׁ֑ן עֵינַ֜יִךְ בְּרֵכ֣וֹת בְּחֶשְׁבּ֗וֹן עַל־שַׁ֙עַר֙ בַּת־רַבִּ֔ים אַפֵּךְ֙ כְּמִגְדַּ֣ל הַלְּבָנ֔וֹן צוֹפֶ֖ה פְּנֵ֥י דַמָּֽשֶׂק׃
Your head crowns you like Carmel,[^7] and the flowing hair of your head is like purple;[^8] a king is held captive in its tresses.[^9]
רֹאשֵׁ֤ךְ עָלַ֙יִךְ֙ כַּכַּרְמֶ֔ל וְדַלַּ֥ת רֹאשֵׁ֖ךְ כָּאַרְגָּמָ֑ן מֶ֖לֶךְ אָס֥וּר בָּרְהָטִֽים׃
How beautiful you are, and how pleasant, O love, with its delights!
מַה־יָּפִית֙ וּמַה־נָּעַ֔מְתְּ אַהֲבָ֖ה בַּתַּֽעֲנוּגִֽים׃
Your stature is like a palm tree, and your breasts are like its clusters.
זֹ֤את קֽוֹמָתֵךְ֙ דָּֽמְתָ֣ה לְתָמָ֔ר וְשָׁדַ֖יִךְ לְאַשְׁכֹּלֽוֹת׃
I said, "I will climb the palm tree; I will take hold of its fruit." Oh, may your breasts be like clusters of the vine, and the fragrance of your breath[^10] like apples,
אָמַ֙רְתִּי֙ אֶעֱלֶ֣ה בְתָמָ֔ר אֹֽחֲזָ֖ה בְּסַנְסִנָּ֑יו וְיִֽהְיוּ־נָ֤א שָׁדַ֙יִךְ֙ כְּאֶשְׁכְּל֣וֹת הַגֶּ֔פֶן וְרֵ֥יחַ אַפֵּ֖ךְ כַּתַּפּוּחִֽים׃
and your mouth[^11] like the best wine, going down smoothly for my beloved,[^12] gliding over the lips of sleepers.[^13]
וְחִכֵּ֕ךְ כְּיֵ֥ין הַטּ֛וֹב הוֹלֵ֥ךְ לְדוֹדִ֖י לְמֵישָׁרִ֑ים דּוֹבֵ֖ב שִׂפְתֵ֥י יְשֵׁנִֽים׃
I am my beloved's, and his desire[^14] is for me.
אֲנִ֣י לְדוֹדִ֔י וְעָלַ֖י תְּשׁוּקָתֽוֹ׃ ס
Come, my beloved, let us go out into the fields; let us spend the night in the villages.[^15]
לְכָ֤ה דוֹדִי֙ נֵצֵ֣א הַשָּׂדֶ֔ה נָלִ֖ינָה בַּכְּפָרִֽים׃
Let us go early to the vineyards; let us see whether the vine has budded, whether its blossoms have opened, whether the pomegranates are in bloom. There I will give you my love.[^16]
נַשְׁכִּ֙ימָה֙ לַכְּרָמִ֔ים נִרְאֶ֞ה אִם[c] פָּֽרְחָ֤ה הַגֶּ֙פֶן֙ פִּתַּ֣ח הַסְּמָדַ֔ר הֵנֵ֖צוּ הָרִמּוֹנִ֑ים שָׁ֛ם אֶתֵּ֥ן אֶת־דֹּדַ֖י לָֽךְ׃
The mandrakes[^17] give out their fragrance, and at our doors are all kinds of choice fruits, new as well as old, which I have stored up for you, my beloved.
הַֽדּוּדָאִ֣ים נָֽתְנוּ־רֵ֗יחַ וְעַל־פְּתָחֵ֙ינוּ֙ כָּל־מְגָדִ֔ים חֲדָשִׁ֖ים גַּם־יְשָׁנִ֑ים דּוֹדִ֖י צָפַ֥נְתִּי לָֽךְ׃

n.1: Verse 1 is 6:13 in most English Bibles, and verses 2–14 are 7:1–13. *Shulammite* may mean "woman of Shulem", perhaps Shunem (1 Kings 1:3), or it may be a feminine form of the name Solomon (*Shelomoh*). Others ("we") speak in the first half of the verse; who answers in the second half is not clear.
n.2: Or "the dance of Mahanaim", a place whose name means "two camps" (Genesis 32:3; 32:2 in most English Bibles).
n.3: Literally "daughter of a noble". The man probably speaks in verses 2–10 ("you" is feminine).
n.4: Wine mixed with spices or water.
n.5: A city east of the Jordan, known for its pools.
n.7: The wooded mountain range on the coast.
n.8: The costly dark red-purple dye worn by kings.
n.9: Hebrew *rehatim*, elsewhere "watering troughs" (Genesis 30:38), here the flowing locks of her hair.
n.12: "My beloved" is the woman's name for the man (1:13). Here she seems to take up the man's words and finish them.
n.13: The Septuagint reads "over my lips and teeth".
n.14: Hebrew *teshuqah*, found elsewhere only in Genesis 3:16 and 4:7.
n.15: Or "among the henna bushes". Hebrew *kefarim* can mean either (compare 1:14).
n.17: Hebrew *duda'im*, a plant believed to stir love and help conception (Genesis 30:14–16). The word sounds like *dodim*, "love", and *dodi*, "my beloved".

v: Oh, that you were like a brother to me,[^1] who nursed at my mother's breasts! If I found you outside, I would kiss you, and no one would despise me.
מִ֤י יִתֶּנְךָ֙ כְּאָ֣ח לִ֔י יוֹנֵ֖ק שְׁדֵ֣י אִמִּ֑י אֶֽמְצָאֲךָ֤ בַחוּץ֙ אֶשָׁ֣קְךָ֔ גַּ֖ם לֹא־יָב֥וּזוּ לִֽי׃
I would lead you, I would bring you into my mother's house; you would teach me.[^2] I would give you spiced wine to drink, the juice of my pomegranates.
אֶנְהָֽגֲךָ֗ אֲבִֽיאֲךָ֛ אֶל־בֵּ֥ית אִמִּ֖י תְּלַמְּדֵ֑נִי אַשְׁקְךָ֙ מִיַּ֣יִן הָרֶ֔קַח מֵעֲסִ֖יס רִמֹּנִֽי׃
His left hand is under my head, and his right hand embraces me.
שְׂמֹאלוֹ֙ תַּ֣חַת רֹאשִׁ֔י וִֽימִינ֖וֹ תְּחַבְּקֵֽנִי׃
I make you swear, daughters of Jerusalem: do not stir up or awaken love until it is ready.[^3]
הִשְׁבַּ֥עְתִּי אֶתְכֶ֖ם בְּנ֣וֹת יְרוּשָׁלָ֑͏ִם מַה־תָּעִ֧ירוּ ׀ וּֽמַה־תְּעֹֽרְר֛וּ אֶת־הָאַהֲבָ֖ה עַ֥ד שֶׁתֶּחְפָּֽץ׃ ס
Who is this coming up from the wilderness, leaning on her beloved?[^4] Under the apple tree I awakened you;[^5] there your mother was in labor with you; there she who bore you was in labor.
מִ֣י זֹ֗את עֹלָה֙ מִן־הַמִּדְבָּ֔ר מִתְרַפֶּ֖קֶת עַל־דּוֹדָ֑הּ תַּ֤חַת הַתַּפּ֙וּחַ֙ עֽוֹרַרְתִּ֔יךָ שָׁ֚מָּה חִבְּלַ֣תְךָ אִמֶּ֔ךָ שָׁ֖מָּה חִבְּלָ֥ה יְלָדַֽתְךָ׃
Set me as a seal on your heart, as a seal on your arm, for love is as strong as death, its passion[^6] as unyielding as Sheol.[^7] Its flashes are flashes of fire, a flame of the LORD.[^8]
שִׂימֵ֨נִי כַֽחוֹתָ֜ם עַל־לִבֶּ֗ךָ כַּֽחוֹתָם֙ עַל־זְרוֹעֶ֔ךָ כִּֽי־עַזָּ֤ה כַמָּ֙וֶת֙ אַהֲבָ֔ה קָשָׁ֥ה כִשְׁא֖וֹל קִנְאָ֑ה רְשָׁפֶ֕יהָ רִשְׁפֵּ֕י אֵ֖שׁ שַׁלְהֶ֥בֶתְיָֽה׃
Many waters cannot quench love, and rivers cannot sweep it away. If a man gave all the wealth of his house for love, he would be utterly despised.[^9]
מַ֣יִם רַבִּ֗ים לֹ֤א יֽוּכְלוּ֙ לְכַבּ֣וֹת אֶת־הָֽאַהֲבָ֔ה וּנְהָר֖וֹת לֹ֣א יִשְׁטְפ֑וּהָ אִם־יִתֵּ֨ן אִ֜ישׁ אֶת־כָּל־ה֤וֹן בֵּיתוֹ֙ בָּאַהֲבָ֔ה בּ֖וֹז יָב֥וּזוּ לֽוֹ׃ ס
We have a little sister, and she has no breasts.[^10] What shall we do for our sister on the day she is spoken for?
אָח֥וֹת לָ֙נוּ֙ קְטַנָּ֔ה וְשָׁדַ֖יִם אֵ֣ין לָ֑הּ מַֽה־נַּעֲשֶׂה֙ לַאֲחֹתֵ֔נוּ בַּיּ֖וֹם שֶׁיְּדֻבַּר־בָּֽהּ׃
If she is a wall, we will build on her a battlement of silver; but if she is a door, we will enclose her with boards of cedar.
אִם־חוֹמָ֣ה הִ֔יא נִבְנֶ֥ה עָלֶ֖יהָ טִ֣ירַת כָּ֑סֶף וְאִם־דֶּ֣לֶת הִ֔יא נָצ֥וּר עָלֶ֖יהָ ל֥וּחַ אָֽרֶז׃
I am a wall, and my breasts are like towers; so I have become in his eyes like one who finds peace.[^11]
אֲנִ֣י חוֹמָ֔ה וְשָׁדַ֖י כַּמִּגְדָּל֑וֹת אָ֛ז הָיִ֥יתִי בְעֵינָ֖יו כְּמוֹצְאֵ֥ת שָׁלֽוֹם׃ פ
Solomon had a vineyard at Baal-hamon;[^12] he gave the vineyard to keepers. Each was to bring for its fruit a thousand pieces of silver.[^13]
כֶּ֣רֶם הָיָ֤ה לִשְׁלֹמֹה֙ בְּבַ֣עַל הָמ֔וֹן נָתַ֥ן אֶת־הַכֶּ֖רֶם לַנֹּטְרִ֑ים אִ֛ישׁ יָבִ֥א בְּפִרְי֖וֹ אֶ֥לֶף כָּֽסֶף׃
My vineyard, my very own, is before me.[^14] The thousand are yours, Solomon, and two hundred for those who keep its fruit.
כַּרְמִ֥י[t] שֶׁלִּ֖י לְפָנָ֑י הָאֶ֤לֶף לְךָ֙ שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה וּמָאתַ֖יִם לְנֹטְרִ֥ים אֶת־פִּרְיֽוֹ׃
You who sit in the gardens, companions are listening for your voice; let me hear it.[^15]
הַיוֹשֶׁ֣בֶת בַּגַּנִּ֗ים חֲבֵרִ֛ים מַקְשִׁיבִ֥ים לְקוֹלֵ֖ךְ הַשְׁמִיעִֽינִי׃
Flee, my beloved, and be like a gazelle or a young stag on the mountains of spices.[^16]
בְּרַ֣ח ׀ דּוֹדִ֗י וּֽדְמֵה־לְךָ֤ לִצְבִי֙ א֚וֹ לְעֹ֣פֶר הָֽאַיָּלִ֔ים עַ֖ל הָרֵ֥י בְשָׂמִֽים׃

n.1: The woman speaks in verses 1–4 ("you" is masculine). Literally "Who would make you like a brother to me".
n.2: Or "she would teach me", that is, my mother. The Septuagint reads "and into the room of the one who conceived me", as in 3:4.
n.3: Literally "why would you stir up and why would you awaken love until it pleases?" Here the refrain has no oath by the gazelles and does (compare 2:7; 3:5).
n.4: Others speak, perhaps the daughters of Jerusalem (compare 3:6). In the rest of verse 5 and in verses 6–7 the woman speaks ("you" is masculine).
n.7: Hebrew *Sheol*, the realm of the dead.
n.8: Hebrew *shalhevetyah*, written as one word in the Leningrad Codex. The ending *-yah* may be *Yah*, the short form of the name YHWH (as in *hallelu-yah*, "praise Yah"; Exodus 15:2), giving "a flame of Yah", "the very flame of the LORD". Or it may express a superlative, "a mighty flame", "the hottest flame", as words for God sometimes do in Hebrew (compare "mountains of God", that is, mighty mountains, in Psalm 36:7; 36:6 in most English Bibles). Some Hebrew manuscripts write it as two words, *shalhevet yah*, "a flame of Yah". If the divine name is here, it is the only place it appears in the Song.
n.10: Perhaps her brothers speak in verses 8–9 (compare 1:6).
n.11: Hebrew *shalom*, "peace", perhaps a play on *Shelomoh*, "Solomon" (verses 11–12), and on "Shulammite" (7:1). The woman speaks.
n.12: The place is not known. The name means "owner of a crowd" or "owner of wealth".
n.13: Literally "a thousand of silver", probably shekels: about 25 pounds (11.5 kg) of silver.
n.14: Compare 1:6. The speaker is probably the woman, perhaps the man.
